overview: This Senate resolution honors Nicholas Douglas Quets, a U.S. Marine Corps veteran from Tucson, Arizona, who was shot and killed on October 18, 2024, while driving through the Mexican state of Sonora. According to the resolution, he was attacked by armed criminals linked to the Sinaloa Cartel, a Mexican drug trafficking organization, at an unauthorized roadside checkpoint run by the cartel. It describes his military service, his later work as a welder on water projects for Pima County, and expresses condolences to his family. The resolution condemns the Sinaloa Cartel and other cross-border criminal groups, recognizes the danger cartel violence poses to Americans traveling abroad, and reaffirms the U.S. commitment to pursuing justice and fighting such groups. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on September 29, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution honors a veteran's service and loss and puts the Senate on record against cartel violence that endangers Americans traveling in Mexico.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it does not change any law or provide new funding or tools to combat cartels.
